scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem that an auto-answering AI agent can resolve, including auto-fixing bills.

H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors (e.g., altered estimate-substitution logic), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI register read delivery/semantic validity from the vendor (ORG-AMI via MDMS) degraded, causing missing or invalid reads that forced estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter read collection or the daily upload handoff from the contracted field service degraded, increasing missed/incomplete reads and estimate substitutions.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A staffing shortage at the contracted field service reduced route completion, directly causing more estimated (incorrect) bills, as the Field Operations Manager would attribute it.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A billing/tariff calculation defect affecting bills built from ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads is driving a large share of disputes, since ACTUAL-read disputes (1785) exceed ESTIMATED-read disputes (1240).

H-HIGHCONSUMP-REJECT.statement: The billing import validation logic rejects AMI reads flagged as high-consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) even when delivered on time, forcing estimate substitution for the large majority (1184/1240) of disputed ESTIMATED-read bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts (9200 accounts) was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over 2026-08..09, the same window as the dispute surge, indicating a measurable shortfall in manual meter-read collection. The record shows the shortfall's existence, not its cause (staffing vs. other handoff failure).

Still shows manual-read route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts over 2026-08..09, i.e. a real field-collection shortfall exists. It no longer supports PR-CHAIN-5/PR-ROOT's claim that this shortfall is a contributor to the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, since E-12 shows those bills are entirely AMI-channel (1184+56=1240), not manual-read field accounts.

Disputed bills break down as 1240 ESTIMATED-read and 1785 ACTUAL-read (total 3025), so the majority of disputed bills involve ACTUAL (not estimated) reads. This means estimate-substitution-based causal theories can at most explain the ESTIMATED subset (~41%), leaving the larger ACTUAL-read share unexplained by read-collection failure alone.

Still shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED / 1785 ACTUAL (total 3025). It no longer supports framing the ESTIMATED subset as plausibly caused by field manual-read collection failure, since E-12 shows all 1240 ESTIMATED disputes trace to AMI-channel reads (1184 rejected at import, 56 never received), undercutting PR-ROOT's framing of E-01's field-route shortfall as a contributor to this subset.

The CRM record shows ticket handling is currently within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs. a 3.0-day target, over 2440 tickets), indicating the surge is not a backlog/response-latency problem at present. This undercuts the premise behind CL-01's framing that an auto-answering agent addressing response speed would resolve the dispute surge; it says nothing about why bills are wrong.

The authoritative, complete billing-db tariff_change_log returns zero records, meaning no tariff rate/structure changes are logged in the system. This rules out a tariff-rule-change event as the mechanism behind any billing calculation defect, narrowing (but not eliminating) the 'billing/tariff calculation defect' theory for ACTUAL-read disputes to causes other than a logged tariff change.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a reader staffing shortage since July is causing late routes, and those late-route customers get estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder claim (NON_AUTHORITATIVE) offering a cause for the already-observed route completion shortfall (E-01), but it does not touch why disputed bills are predominantly ACTUAL-read (E-02).

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year, a stakeholder claim that agrees with the already-recorded authoritative value from E-04 (tariff_change_log has zero records). This is corroborating but non-authoritative; it adds no new mechanism and does not touch the still-unexplained ACTUAL-read dispute majority (E-02).

Monthly dispute ticket counts (610 Jun, 590 Jul, 1180 Aug, 1260 Sep) show volume roughly doubling from July to August and staying elevated in September, corroborating the magnitude/timing of the surge CL-01 describes. The record only shows aggregate ticket counts over time; it carries no information about read type, cause, or whether tickets are resolved correctly, so it does not discriminate between competing causal hypotheses.

Still shows aggregate monthly dispute ticket counts (610/590/1180/1260) roughly doubling from July to August and staying elevated in September, with no information on read type or cause. It no longer can be treated as corroborating a field-staffing/manual-read-driven mechanism for the ESTIMATED-read portion of that surge, since E-12 shows the ESTIMATED subset's timing is explained by AMI-channel import rejection, not field route completion shortfalls (E-01).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document establishes that the utility may request field route priority changes but that execution requires confirmation from the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), confirming the contractual basis for the human-approval gate already modeled as K-DISPATCH on push_route_update. It speaks to authorization/process for a protected action, not to the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log lagging_routes query returns 14 routes with below-target completion (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity under the aggregate 0.88 completion shortfall already recorded in E-01. It shows which routes are lagging but not why, so it does not discriminate between the staffing-shortage and handoff-failure causal theories left open by U-FIELDCAUSE.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: This billing-db query shows 320 accounts received estimated bills last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (E-10). It links billing-side estimation to specific field routes but gives no overlap with the 14 lagging routes already identified (E-09), so it does not tell us which routes' shortfalls actually produced the estimated bills.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI claims (unverified, NON_AUTHORITATIVE) that MDMS export access for Lakeside was provisioned today per vendor ticket TX-4471. If accurate, this unblocks the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated query, but it says nothing about whether AMI read delivery itself was degraded.

For the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, mdms-export shows 1184 had an AMI read delivered before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 had no AMI read received at all. This indicates AMI vendor delivery itself is largely intact and the dominant driver of these estimate substitutions is a billing-side import rejection rule, not AMI delivery degradation or field manual-read failure.

U-METRICVALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Use the aggregate monthly volume as an interim target while also tracking the ACTUAL-read dispute share as a secondary check.
